findings.claim: The delegated resume sets keeper.Fingerprint to delegatedSelectionFingerprint, and ResumeDelegated hands that keeper to ContinueDelegated, so the start-time fingerprint and barren reads use the selection's hold reader; landing run passes it to the selection only.
findings.evidence: intent_landing_resume.go:35 assigns the wrapper; resume.go:53 copies *s.ResumeKeeper and :89 continues with it; lane/agent.go:351 records k.Fingerprint(root) at start. A probe in TestLandingResumeRunsUnderARecordedDelegation/paused=false recorded "unchanged", so no effect was observed in the bed; if a hold reports at start, the launch records an empty fingerprint and countBarren skips it.
findings.change: Pass the selection reader to ResumeDelegated separately, or restore the keeper's own fingerprint before ContinueDelegated.
findings.relation: the continuation keeps the keeper's own fingerprint reader; the selection reader serves the selection only

findings.claim: Kind "resume" passed to ResumeDelegated is overwritten with "selection" by selectRecordedBatch, so the recorded batch cannot tell a delegated resume from a delegated landing run --goals.
findings.evidence: batch.go selectRecordedBatch sets d.Kind = "selection"; RecordedDelegatedBatch (batch.go:318) requires Kind == "selection". The decision log still names the argv.
findings.change: Either record the act kind separately or drop the dead Kind value from the command; this is base behaviour that C7's wording did not account for.

findings.claim: pendingSelection now appends the reason to the summary while keeping it as Details[0], so text output repeats it, for person selections too.
findings.evidence: intent_landing.go:1248; this keeps U1b2a's T3c(a) 'the line names the provider hold' true after the delegated provider row moved to the saved report; TestAuditOutputLayout* passed.
findings.change: Drop the reason from Details when it is in the summary, or leave it as is.

findings.claim: T3e's oldest-first order does not depend on ResumeDelegated's sort: the bed queues older before newer, so removing SortStableFunc would not fail the held row.
findings.evidence: resume_test.go:154 held row expects [older, newer]; b.queue writes them in that order, and Waiting returns them in time order already.
findings.change: Queue the newer goal first with an earlier-looking file order, or give the entries out-of-order At values.
findings.relation: each asserted property has a row that fails without it
